title: Proposed: control plane / data plane — tenants own many databases

elements.name: Database platform
elements.description: Control plane manages tenant databases. Data plane routes queries to database owner nodes.

elements.name: Customer administrator
elements.description: Creates tenants and databases, inspects state and requests database lifecycle operations.

elements.name: Customer query client
elements.description: One session can address any authorized database of its tenant by name or ID through the same query endpoint.

elements.name: Database backup store
elements.description: Verified snapshots per database ID and generation. Optional WAL frames are future work.

elements.name: Control plane
elements.description: Manage tenants and their databases: CRUD, configuration, provisioning and lifecycle.

elements.name: Data plane
elements.description: One query endpoint. Authorize database selection, resolve placement and return results.

elements.name: Postgres metadata
elements.description: Tenants, databases, placement epochs and durable operations. Hand-written SQL; no ORM.

elements.name: Node agent + supervisor
elements.description: Validate database epochs, manage files and supervise child-process statement lanes.

elements.name: Statement lanes
elements.description: Proposed child processes. Per-database handles, queues and request-ID state; landed FFI code.

elements.name: Database SQLite files
elements.description: One file and WAL/SHM set per database. Separate transactions and writer locks.

elements.name: Management ingress
elements.description: Authenticate administrators. Check permissions. Record idempotent operations and return status.

elements.name: Tenant registry
elements.description: Create, configure and inspect tenants. Drop only after all owned databases are deleted.

elements.name: Database registry
elements.description: Tenant-scoped database CRUD, configure and inspect. Immutable IDs; names are not paths.

elements.name: Database provisioner
elements.description: Select a node, create and verify one database file, then publish its active placement.

elements.name: Database lifecycle
elements.description: Move, suspend/resume, backup/restore and delete. Fence and drain before changing ownership.

elements.name: Query ingress
elements.description: Select any authorized database by name/ID through the same endpoint and session; return results.

elements.name: Session + database auth
elements.description: Derive trusted tenant identity. Verify database ownership and grants for each selection.

elements.name: Placement router
elements.description: Database → node and epoch at open. Refresh after moves. Database-aware seam extension is planned.
plannedNotes: The TenantStorageRouter interface is landed; database-aware ControlPlaneRouter, gateway placement and remote execution are planned.

elements.name: Owner-node forwarder
elements.description: Forward trusted tenant/database IDs, epoch, request ID, operation IR, SQL/binds and deadline.

elements.name: Admission + supervisor
elements.description: Check database state/epoch per request. Gate, drain and close handles before acknowledging a fence.

elements.name: Statement classifier
elements.description: Landed operation-IR classifier: bounded blocking path or unbounded nonblocking read.

elements.name: FFI statement executor
elements.description: Landed scoped libsqlite3 execution. Reused in proposed lanes; no separate library container.

elements.name: Deadline / interrupt
elements.description: Landed interrupt and settlement. Lane watchdog escalation and database-drain integration are proposed.
plannedNotes: Lane watchdog escalation and database-scoped drain acknowledgement are proposed.

documents.title: Database platform: control plane + data plane
documents.plain:
Management uses the control plane. Queries use the data plane. Both address databases by tenant and database identity; clients never select a hosting node.

A tenant owns zero or more databases (0..N). The database is the unit of placement, isolation, backup and lifecycle. One-file-per-tenant is superseded in this proposal; the lanes dataset stays unchanged.

ste.text:
Use the control plane to manage databases. Use the data plane to query a database. The service selects its node.

A tenant can have zero or more databases. Place, isolate, back up and manage each database separately. This proposal replaces one file for each tenant with one file for each database. The lanes dataset does not change.

documents.title: Customer administrator
documents.plain:
Creates tenants and databases, inspects state and requests database lifecycle operations.

A tenant owns zero or more databases (0..N). The database is the unit of placement, isolation, backup and lifecycle. One-file-per-tenant is superseded in this proposal; the lanes dataset stays unchanged.

ste.text:
Create or remove tenants and databases. Inspect their state. Request a move or a backup.

A tenant can have zero or more databases. Place, isolate, back up and manage each database separately. This proposal replaces one file for each tenant with one file for each database. The lanes dataset does not change.

documents.title: Customer query client
documents.plain:
One session can address any authorized database of its tenant by name or ID through the same query endpoint.

A tenant owns zero or more databases (0..N). The database is the unit of placement, isolation, backup and lifecycle. One-file-per-tenant is superseded in this proposal; the lanes dataset stays unchanged.

ste.text:
Use the same endpoint and session to query any database that you are permitted to use.

A tenant can have zero or more databases. Place, isolate, back up and manage each database separately. This proposal replaces one file for each tenant with one file for each database. The lanes dataset does not change.

documents.title: Per-database backup store
documents.plain:
Proposed verified snapshots and optional later WAL frames, keyed by immutable database ID and generation. Retention and erasure are explicit per-database policies.

A tenant owns zero or more databases (0..N). The database is the unit of placement, isolation, backup and lifecycle. One-file-per-tenant is superseded in this proposal; the lanes dataset stays unchanged.

documents.title: Move database: fence, copy, then flip placement
documents.plain:
Design choice: an offline, per-database move with temporary unavailability. The source must acknowledge a durable fence; otherwise placement does not flip. Recovery reads durable MOVING state before reopening any file. Only after in-flight work settles, all handles close, and target data verifies does one Postgres transaction publish the new ACTIVE epoch. Target admits only after that commit. Source remains fenced even after restart. Cleanup follows activation; its failure never re-enables the old owner. Other databases can remain active, except for the documented shared-lane kill blast radius. Snapshot copy uses a closed/checkpointed database, not a live main-file-only copy; online WAL streaming is deferred.

A failure after placement commit cannot use this rollback: target remains the sole owner and the controller reconciles activation/cleanup, or runs a new fenced move.

documents.title: Suspend, resume, backup and restore
documents.plain:
Suspend uses the same per-database gate and drain as move; SUSPENDED blocks opens and existing-session admissions. Resume requires verified file readiness, ACTIVE state and a fresh epoch. Backup takes a consistent per-database SQLite backup with an identity/generation manifest and verification; it does not copy a live main file alone. Restore stages and verifies a backup before a fenced, drained generation swap and fresh-epoch activation. IDs/authorization must still match; restoring data cannot resurrect deleted grants. Operations use durable IDs and state transitions, never a distributed transaction across SQL and files. This design chooses temporary unavailability and reconciliation over unproven online relocation or failover.

A tenant owns zero or more databases (0..N). The database is the unit of placement, isolation, backup and lifecycle. One-file-per-tenant is superseded in this proposal; the lanes dataset stays unchanged.

ste.text:
Suspend one database by stopping admission and draining work. Resume it only when its file is verified. Make and verify a consistent database backup. For restore, stop access and verify staged data before replacing the generation. Change the epoch before resuming access. Keep operation records so work can resume after a crash.
